BiblicalUsage: A valley is the low ground between hills, where harvests are reaped and battles are fought — the men of Beth-shemesh were reaping in the valley when the ark came back in 1 Samuel 6:13, and Jehoshaphat's people blessed the LORD in the valley of Berachah in 2 Chronicles 20:26. The Syrians claimed the LORD was only God of the hills, but in 1 Kings 20:28 He proves Himself God of the valleys too.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the valley is where most of life is actually lived — not on the mountain tops but down in the low places — and I hold that God meets us there just as surely as on the heights. The valley of Berachah was named for blessing because God's people praised Him there before the battle was even over, and that is the pattern I want for my own low places.
